feature1.prompt: The SequentialFeatureSelector currently fails when provided with an iterable of splits for the cv parameter. Although using cv as an integer (for example, cv=5) works properly, passing an iterable of splits is expected to run without errors according to the documentation. The issue appears to be related to how the cv parameter is validated and processed in the fit method. The fix should ensure that the cv parameter, including generators or iterables of splits, is correctly accepted and converted so that the estimator can use it without error.
feature1.hint_texts: Focus on modifying the fit method within SequentialFeatureSelector. Integrate the check_cv utility to properly validate and process the cv parameter. The changes should occur before any internal methods are invoked so that a validated cv object is available for further use. This adjustment is isolated to input validation and parameter setup.
feature1.entrypoint: File: sklearn/feature_selection/_sequential.py; Function: fit; Modify the section before cloning the estimator to include 'cv = check_cv(self.cv, y, classifier=is_classifier(self.estimator))'.

tests.PASS_TO_PASS: sklearn/feature_selection/tests/test_sequential.py::test_bad_n_features_to_select and the other tests that verify n_features_to_select functionality

feature2.prompt: SequentialFeatureSelector's internal feature evaluation logic does not currently use the validated cv parameter for scoring. Even after the cv parameter is correctly processed in the fit method, the _get_best_new_feature_score function continues to reference the original cv attribute. This leads to issues when iterables of splits are provided, resulting in errors during feature selection. The fix should update the internal scoring method to accept and use the validated cv parameter, ensuring the feature selection process works as expected without errors.
feature2.hint_texts: Focus on updating the _get_best_new_feature_score method in the SequentialFeatureSelector. Modify the function signature to accept an extra parameter for the validated cv and pass this parameter to the scoring function. Adjust the call within the iterative feature selection loop in the fit method so that the validated cv is forwarded correctly. This part addresses the core of the feature scoring logic inside the selector.
feature2.entrypoint: File: sklearn/feature_selection/_sequential.py; Function: _get_best_new_feature_score; Change the function to include 'cv' in its parameters and update the call to cross_val_score to use the validated 'cv'.

tests.PASS_TO_PASS: All tests that previously passed (e.g., test_n_features_to_select variations, test_sanity tests, etc.) ensuring overall selector functionality remain passing

collaboration_points.shared_resources: File: sklearn/feature_selection/_sequential.py, particularly the SequentialFeatureSelector class and its methods; shared utilities such as check_cv and cross_val_score.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Feature1 will implement the change in the fit method to validate and assign the cv parameter using check_cv. Feature2 will modify _get_best_new_feature_score to use this validated cv for scoring. Both features must coordinate to ensure that the validated cv is consistently propagated from the fit method into the internal feature scoring logic, maintaining compatibility with the cross-validation API.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers working on Feature1 and Feature2 should discuss the exact format and expectations of the validated cv object. They need to establish clear integration points to verify that the cv parameter initialized in fit is the same one used in _get_best_new_feature_score. Regular check-ins and integration tests will be essential to ensure the cohesive behavior of the SequentialFeatureSelector.
